feature: Canonical library title ordering with deterministic original-path ties
regression_before_fix: The initial same-directory reproducer placed a decomposed accented title before z, while equivalent composed titles followed z. The final regression places equivalent titles in separate folders to avoid same-directory case-equivalent filename requirements.
implementation: Stable original-path sort followed by stable cached title-key sort using the same NFC/lowercase/NFC key as library search. No path clones are added to the cached title keys.
assertions: Consistent uncached, cold-cache and warm-cache order
Canonical title ties resolved by original path
Recreating source files in reverse order retains display order and four cache hits
Original filenames, metadata titles and content bytes preserved
Canonical search still finds both title representations
commands: nix-shell --run 'cargo fmt --all && cargo test --locked -p femto-reader --lib --test library --test ui && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features desktop,femto-catalog/tailnet --locked -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all --check'

firmware_manifest.installation_status: No automatic installer. Verify the actual device partition table and recovery backup before installation.

limitations: Unicode key ordering is not locale-specific collation
Truncated traversal can retain a different subset when directory enumeration changes
No new full workspace/native/independent-peer suite or grayscale build
Physical device memory and latency remain unqualified
